newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt knocked down by French elections.
newsitem.headline: German debt knocked down by French elections.

text.p: German debt was jolted lower on Monday as France swung to the left in a first round of parliamentary elections but dealers predicted the market's attention would soon shift back to U.S. Treasury market moves.

Germany's June Bund futures contract ended trading down 25 basis points at 100.70, its session low, having spent the session in a relatively narrow 100.83 to 100.70 range. At the same time the cash bond was trading at 100.49, down from Friday's close of 100.79. There was little late reaction to news France's prime minister Alain Juppe would resign regardless of the election outcome.

Investors began backing out of German debt early in the session following the French market's slide on fears a left-wing victory in France might prompt the government to appeal to European partner nations that the entry criteria for monetary union might be softened.
Dealers said that French markets in particular are expected to remain nervous until Sunday's final vote.
But there was also talk that investors, holding spare cash, would be tempted to buy on dips which could help underpin the French bond market and support the German market by extension.

Bunds, which had ticked higher late last week, as investors swapped into the German market on fears over the outcome of the French election, might move higher again if the U.S. market permits, dealers said.
Thin volumes on Monday, prompted by bank holidays in the U.S. and the U.K. may have held the market back, dealers said.

The direction might however be determined by those markets' reactions to the French vote, dealers said, adding that Tuesday's release of April home sales and the May consumer confidence index in the U.S. might also affect the market.
The week's highlight in the U.S. however the release of durable goods orders in April as well as May's Chicago Purchasing Manager Index.
